g.text: YF-G1 flow sensor, relay-switched 12 V DC solenoid valve, 433 MHz remote, ESP data out

g.desc: YF-G1 flow sensor, relay-switched 12 V DC solenoid valve, 433 MHz remote, ESP data out

g.text: Pins: D2 flow, D4 button, D5-D7 LEDs, D8 relay, D11 ESP, A0-A3 remote

g.desc: Pins: D2 flow, D4 button, D5-D7 LEDs, D8 relay, D11 ESP, A0-A3 remote

g.text: J2: run the valve +12 V and return as their own pair,

g.desc: J2: run the valve +12 V and return as their own pair,

g.text: and keep them away from the sensor and remote cables.

g.desc: and keep them away from the sensor and remote cables.

g.text: ESP DATA OUT (9600 baud, 3.3 V level)

g.desc: ESP DATA OUT (9600 baud, 3.3 V level)

g.text: D12 is reserved for a future ESP -> Nano link.

g.desc: D12 is reserved for a future ESP -> Nano link.

g.text: Nano is powered through its 5V pin (VIN unused).

g.desc: Nano is powered through its 5V pin (VIN unused).

g.text: 1. D2 flyback diode right at the valve terminals (stripe to +).

g.desc: 1. D2 flyback diode right at the valve terminals (stripe to +).

g.text: 2. Valve current has its own wire pair (J2) back to J1: star ground at J1.

g.desc: 2. Valve current has its own wire pair (J2) back to J1: star ground at J1.

g.text: 3. Decoupling: C1 + C2 on 12 V, C3 + C4 at U1, C12 at the Nano, C6 at J4.

g.desc: 3. Decoupling: C1 + C2 on 12 V, C3 + C4 at U1, C12 at the Nano, C6 at J4.

g.text: 4. Flow input: R1 10k pull-up, R2 1k + C5 10nF filter, firmware glitch filter.

g.desc: 4. Flow input: R1 10k pull-up, R2 1k + C5 10nF filter, firmware glitch filter.

g.text: 5. Button and remote inputs: 10k pull-ups + 100nF, firmware debounce.

g.desc: 5. Button and remote inputs: 10k pull-ups + 100nF, firmware debounce.

g.text: 6. F1 fuse + D1 crowbar protect against shorts and a reversed supply.

g.desc: 6. F1 fuse + D1 crowbar protect against shorts and a reversed supply.

g.text: 7. R11 / R12 divide the 5 V data line down to 3.2 V for the ESP.

g.desc: 7. R11 / R12 divide the 5 V data line down to 3.2 V for the ESP.

g.text: 8. Twist each sensor / remote signal with its GND; route away from valve wires.

g.desc: 8. Twist each sensor / remote signal with its GND; route away from valve wires.

g.text: 9. Ground plane on the PCB bottom layer; keep the 12 V valve tracks short and wide.

g.desc: 9. Ground plane on the PCB bottom layer; keep the 12 V valve tracks short and wide.

g.text: OFF-BOARD WIRING (connects to J2-J5; these parts are not placed on the PCB)

g.desc: OFF-BOARD WIRING (connects to J2-J5; these parts are not placed on the PCB)

g.text: Valve circuit: relay COM <- J2 pin 1 (+12 V), valve - -> J2 pin 2.

g.desc: Valve circuit: relay COM <- J2 pin 1 (+12 V), valve - -> J2 pin 2.

g.text: D2 sits on the valve terminals.

g.desc: D2 sits on the valve terminals.

g.text: FLOW SENSOR INPUT (YF-G1, NPN open collector)

g.desc: FLOW SENSOR INPUT (YF-G1, NPN open collector)

g.text: REMOTE RECEIVER INPUTS (433 MHz, 4 relay channels)

g.desc: REMOTE RECEIVER INPUTS (433 MHz, 4 relay channels)

g.text: R2 + C5 filter fast spikes (time constant 10 us);

g.desc: R2 + C5 filter fast spikes (time constant 10 us);

g.text: the firmware also ignores pulses < 2 ms apart.

g.desc: the firmware also ignores pulses < 2 ms apart.

g.text: POWER: 12 V IN, FUSE, REVERSE-POLARITY CROWBAR, 5 V REGULATOR

g.desc: POWER: 12 V IN, FUSE, REVERSE-POLARITY CROWBAR, 5 V REGULATOR

g.text: F1 + D1: if the supply is connected backwards, D1 conducts and blows F1.

g.desc: F1 + D1: if the supply is connected backwards, D1 conducts and blows F1.

g.text: U1: L7805 needs a small heatsink. Once an ESP is fitted, use a pin-compatible

g.desc: U1: L7805 needs a small heatsink. Once an ESP is fitted, use a pin-compatible

g.text: switching regulator (e.g. R-78E5.0-1.0) or a 5 V buck module wired to IN / GND / OUT.

g.desc: switching regulator (e.g. R-78E5.0-1.0) or a 5 V buck module wired to IN / GND / OUT.

g.text: Remote: all COM terminals to GND, NO1-NO4 to J5 pins 3-6.

g.desc: Remote: all COM terminals to GND, NO1-NO4 to J5 pins 3-6.

g.text: +12 V board shown; power a 5 V board from +5V instead.

g.desc: +12 V board shown; power a 5 V board from +5V instead.
